how: WEA Sydney runs ten-plus in-person Spanish courses from beginner A1 to advanced C1 conversation at its Bathurst Street centre.
The Australian Museum at 1 William Street is open daily with free general entry and permanent natural history exhibitions.
The University of Sydney publishes its online courses and specialisations on Coursera, open to learners anywhere, and Open Universities Australia lists thousands of online subjects.
WEA Sydney runs a Philosophy Club course and other philosophy discussion courses in person, and Meetup lists open philosophical discussion nights at Humanist House.
Northern Beaches Council libraries list an Open Mic Night among adult programs, and Meetup lists open mic nights such as Soultrap in Surry Hills; dedicated poetry slams are not shown.

WEA Sydney's One Night Only evening talks (for example Agatha Christie, Cinema of the 1970s and an Elvis evening) run on Friday nights at its Bathurst Street centre, and the University of Sydney hosts the Sydney Ideas public lecture series.
Sydney Observatory (Powerhouse) at Millers Point is open Thursday to Sunday, and Powerhouse Castle Hill and the new Parramatta museum cover science, design and technology.
The City of Sydney's free Sydney Culture Walks app offers seven self-guided walks, including Hidden laneways, Chinatown to Circular Quay, and the Yananurala Walking on Country trail.
Many Toastmasters clubs meet across Sydney, including Burwood, Drummoyne (Club 5 Dock), Chatswood Communicators, Epping and Dundas.
The Anzac Memorial in Hyde Park is a heritage-listed war memorial and museum, and Cockatoo Island and Fort Denison offer guided harbour-heritage tours.

Cat Protection Society of NSW recruits adult volunteers for shelter care, foster care and the cattery at Enmore Road, Newtown, though shelter-care applications were closed as of February 2026 and waiting lists are common.
Take 3 For The Sea runs community programs encouraging beach and waterway clean-ups, and Meetup lists Dive Against Debris clean-up dives in Sydney.
venue: Take 3 For The Sea / Dive Against Debris

how: A one-off Ice Baths and Wellness Brand pop-up was listed at Beach Road Hotel in North Bondi; regular cold-plunge venues were not confirmed.
The City of Sydney lists 22 community gardens (for example Glebe Community Gardens, Newtown Community Garden, Sydney City Farm in St Peters) that residents can join.
The City of Sydney lists 50+ off-leash dog areas, including Sydney Park (Alexandria), Moore Park, Prince Alfred Park and Wentworth Park.

Sydney Mechanics' School of Arts runs member hobby groups (social chess, bridge, canasta and games, knitting, crafty connections, French conversation), and Meetup lists Sydney interest groups such as Aussie Explorers walking and Sydney Street Photographers.

how: Sydney Community College runs Massage Course for Beginners (levels 1 and 2) at its Rozelle campus.
Sydney Community College runs a Calm Mind meditation course for beginners in Rozelle.
Raise Foundation runs youth mentoring programs (in-school, digital and community) from its Sydney head office, recruiting volunteer mentors.
No natural hot springs in the Sydney area; the nearest are the artesian hot spring baths at Moree, about 628 km north-west (roughly 8 hours by road or a short flight).
AAPES in Botany is a warehouse parkour and freerunning gym with year-round classes including first-timers sessions, and Ninja Parc in South Granville also runs parkour classes.
Cat Protection Society of NSW runs an adoption centre in Newtown (by appointment after an online questionnaire); RSPCA NSW (Yagoona) and others also list adoptions.
Studio Pilates on Bathurst Street offers 40-minute reformer classes through the day, alongside other CBD studios such as PilatesBarre and City Physio & Pilates.
Sydney Community College runs a Qi Gong Course for Beginners at its Rozelle campus; a free online and Parramatta tai chi and qigong group also meets via Meetup.
Active Locals hosts social group runs through Meetup (for example Tuesday 6pm Darling Harbour and Wednesday Manly runs).
Bondi Icebergs Club's ocean pool complex has a sauna (its cleaning schedule lists daily sauna closure), alongside the pool open to the public.
Alcoholics Anonymous Australia operates an online and in-person meeting finder, with groups meeting across NSW including Sydney.
Sydney Community College runs Tai Chi courses for beginners and continuers in Rozelle.
Sze Yup Temple (Kwan Ti temple, 1898-1904) in Glebe is an active Taoist temple serving the Chinese community and hosting celebrations such as Chinese New Year.
Guided after-dark Dark Past tour of Cockatoo Island's Dog Leg Tunnel, convict workshops and Biloela House; guided only, no unsupervised exploration.
Sydney City Farm in St Peters runs volunteer working bees (after an induction session) and Cat Protection Society of NSW recruits adult volunteers, alongside event volunteering listed on Eventbrite.
Sydney Community College runs Gentle Yoga for Wellness courses in Rozelle and a free Hatha yoga intro workshop.
Bullfighting is not practised in Australia (illegal in most countries); the nearest traditions are in Spain, Portugal, southern France and Latin America, a full day or more of travel away.
Two full-size cable wakeboard lakes with learn-to-ride sessions and kids' programs inside the Panthers complex.
No canyons within the metro area; the nearest canyoning is in the Blue Mountains, roughly 100 km west (about 2 hours by road).
No flooded natural cave systems exist around Sydney's sandstone basin; the nearest recognised water-filled caves and sinkholes are at Mount Gambier, South Australia, over 1,000 km away.
No caves open for adventure caving in the metro area; the nearest is Jenolan Caves, about 175 km west (roughly 3 hours by road), which offers abseiling and adventure cave tours.
Introductory clay shooting (trap, DTL, skeet) for unlicensed shooters with coaching, equipment and temporary licensing included.
Needs reliable snow; Sydney has none, and the nearest snowfields are Perisher and the Kosciuszko National Park around Jindabyne, roughly 5-6 hours away by road and winter only.
No glaciers in mainland Australia; the nearest guided glacier walks are at Franz Josef, New Zealand (heli-hikes), a trans-Tasman flight plus onward travel of most of a day.
Treetops Adventure St Ives runs self-guided tree ropes courses 1-15 m above ground with swinging bridges and cargo nets, graded from beginner to expert; the park is about 30 minutes from the CBD.
No alpine terrain near Sydney; the nearest high mountains are the Snowy Mountains (Mount Kosciuszko, 2,228 m, a walk-up summit), roughly 5-6 hours by road to Jindabyne.
Open-air tandem skydives over the beach at Stuart Park, North Wollongong, with coach transfers from Sydney CBD (about 1 hour); no drop zone within the metro area.
No suitable flying hills inside the metro area; the nearest and best-known hang gliding and paragliding site is Stanwell Park (Bald Hill), about 59 km south of Sydney, roughly an hour's drive.
No wild-animal safari in the Sydney area; the nearest open-range experience is Taronga Western Plains Zoo in Dubbo, about 400 km west (roughly 5 hours by road), and true safaris are in Africa.
No large dunes or desert near Sydney; the nearest big mobile dunes are at Stockton Bight near Newcastle, roughly 2.5 hours north by road.
A 30-minute instructor-led session on The Avalanche ski and snowboard simulator, with boot hire and a one-on-one warm-up.
No snow fields near Sydney; the nearest resorts are Thredbo and Perisher in the Snowy Mountains, about 500 km south (roughly 6 hours by road, or a flight to Cooma).
No volcanoes within reach of Sydney; volcano boarding is done at Cerro Negro (Nicaragua) and Mount Yasur (Vanuatu, the closest, a flight of several hours).
Ziplines are part of the tree ropes courses at Treetops Adventure St Ives (Showgrounds, Mona Vale Rd).
